paraphrase: These five great sacrifices are spread out and completed continually: to the gods, the ancestors, beings, men and Brahman. When one offers in the fire, even a stick of fuel, that is the sacrifice to the gods; when one offers svadhā to the ancestors, even water, the sacrifice to the ancestors; and so on for beings, men and Brahman (self-study).

paraphrase: At the twilights the knowers of Brahman, facing east, throw up water consecrated with the Gāyatrī; the waters become thunderbolts and hurl the demons called Mandehas onto the island Aruṇa; walking around sunwise they shake off evil; meditating on the rising and setting sun as 'yonder sun is Brahman', the knowing brāhmaṇa attains all good, and being Brahman goes to Brahman.

paraphrase: The wind-girdled seers (vātaraśana ṛṣayaḥ) were śramaṇas who kept their seed drawn upward; the other seers came to them for their purpose; they hid in the kūṣmāṇḍa formulas, and the seers found them there by faith and austerity.

paraphrase: The funeral chapter (pitṛmedha): mantras for laying out and cremating the dead, sending him by the ancient paths to the ancestors and to Yama, collecting the bones and the concluding rites of the survivors.
